questions.question: Under first-past-the-post (FPTP), who wins a constituency?
options: The candidate with the most votes, even without a majority
The party with the most members
The candidate chosen by the courts
questions.explanation: Under FPTP the candidate with the most votes in a single-member constituency wins, even with less than 50% of the vote.

questions.question: Which electoral system tends to produce more proportional parliaments?
questions.explanation: PR produces more representative parliaments but may require coalition governments; FPTP can be highly disproportionate.

questions.question: Which of these is a form of conventional political participation?
options: Voting and joining a political party
questions.explanation: Conventional participation includes voting, joining a party, contacting representatives and running for office.

questions.question: A disadvantage of FPTP is that it can:
options: Produce disproportionate results that underrepresent smaller parties
Guarantee equal seats for every party
questions.explanation: FPTP can produce highly disproportionate results and underrepresent smaller parties, with many "wasted" votes.

questions.question: What does a healthy democracy require beyond elections?
questions.explanation: A healthy democracy requires ongoing engagement — protests, petitions, party involvement — not just voting at elections.
